/- Isolated foundation: no Mathlib and no pre-existing homomorphism API. -/
namespace Foundation

structure Group (G : Type) where
  one : G
  mul : G → G → G
  inv : G → G
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  mul_assoc : ∀ x y z, mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)
  inv_mul : ∀ x, mul (inv x) x = one

def kernelMulGoal : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) (g : Group G) (h : Group H)
    (f : G → H) (hf : ∀ x y, f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y))
    (x y : G), f x = h.one → f y = h.one → f (g.mul x y) = h.one

end Foundation

import Base

namespace Theory

structure Hom {G H : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (h : Foundation.Group H) where
  toFun : G → H
  map_mul : ∀ x y, toFun (g.mul x y) = h.mul (toFun x) (toFun y)

def kernel {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) (x : G) : Prop :=
  f.toFun x = h.one

def Kernel {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : Type :=
  { x : G // kernel f x }

theorem kernel_mul {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) {x y : G} (hx : kernel f x) (hy : kernel f y) :
    kernel f (g.mul x y) := by
  change f.toFun (g.mul x y) = h.one
  calc
    f.toFun (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := f.map_mul x y
    _ = h.mul h.one (f.toFun y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f.toFun y)) hx
    _ = h.mul h.one h.one := congrArg (fun z => h.mul h.one z) hy
    _ = h.one := h.one_mul h.one

def Kernel.mul {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    {f : Hom g h} (x y : Kernel f) : Kernel f :=
  ⟨g.mul x.val y.val, kernel_mul f x.property y.property⟩

end Theory

import Candidate

/- A proved extension of the unchanged v1 package, over the same left-inverse
   foundation. Every helper below is part of the charged v2 package. -/
namespace Theory

namespace GroupFacts

theorem left_cancel {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (a b c : G)
    (e : g.mul a b = g.mul a c) : b = c := by
  calc
    b = g.mul g.one b := (g.one_mul b).symm
    _ = g.mul (g.mul (g.inv a) a) b :=
      congrArg (fun z => g.mul z b) (g.inv_mul a).symm
    _ = g.mul (g.inv a) (g.mul a b) := g.mul_assoc (g.inv a) a b
    _ = g.mul (g.inv a) (g.mul a c) := congrArg (g.mul (g.inv a)) e
    _ = g.mul (g.mul (g.inv a) a) c := (g.mul_assoc (g.inv a) a c).symm
    _ = g.mul g.one c := congrArg (fun z => g.mul z c) (g.inv_mul a)
    _ = c := g.one_mul c

theorem mul_inv {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (x : G) :
    g.mul x (g.inv x) = g.one := by
  apply left_cancel g (g.inv x)
  calc
    g.mul (g.inv x) (g.mul x (g.inv x)) =
        g.mul (g.mul (g.inv x) x) (g.inv x) :=
      (g.mul_assoc (g.inv x) x (g.inv x)).symm
    _ = g.mul g.one (g.inv x) := congrArg (fun z => g.mul z (g.inv x)) (g.inv_mul x)
    _ = g.inv x := g.one_mul (g.inv x)
    _ = g.mul (g.inv x) g.one := (g.mul_one (g.inv x)).symm

theorem inv_one {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) : g.inv g.one = g.one :=
  (g.mul_one (g.inv g.one)).symm.trans (g.inv_mul g.one)

end GroupFacts

theorem Hom.map_one {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : f.toFun g.one = h.one := by
  apply GroupFacts.left_cancel h (f.toFun g.one)
  calc
    h.mul (f.toFun g.one) (f.toFun g.one) = f.toFun (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
      (f.map_mul g.one g.one).symm
    _ = f.toFun g.one := congrArg f.toFun (g.one_mul g.one)
    _ = h.mul (f.toFun g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f.toFun g.one)).symm

theorem Hom.map_inv {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) (x : G) : f.toFun (g.inv x) = h.inv (f.toFun x) := by
  apply GroupFacts.left_cancel h (f.toFun x)
  calc
    h.mul (f.toFun x) (f.toFun (g.inv x)) = f.toFun (g.mul x (g.inv x)) :=
      (f.map_mul x (g.inv x)).symm
    _ = f.toFun g.one := congrArg f.toFun (GroupFacts.mul_inv g x)
    _ = h.one := f.map_one
    _ = h.mul (f.toFun x) (h.inv (f.toFun x)) :=
      (GroupFacts.mul_inv h (f.toFun x)).symm

theorem kernel_one {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : kernel f g.one := f.map_one

theorem kernel_inv {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) {x : G} (hx : kernel f x) : kernel f (g.inv x) := by
  change f.toFun (g.inv x) = h.one
  calc
    f.toFun (g.inv x) = h.inv (f.toFun x) := f.map_inv x
    _ = h.inv h.one := congrArg h.inv hx
    _ = h.one := GroupFacts.inv_one h

def Kernel.group {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : Foundation.Group (Kernel f) where
  one := ⟨g.one, kernel_one f⟩
  mul := Kernel.mul
  inv := fun x => ⟨g.inv x.val, kernel_inv f x.property⟩
  one_mul := fun x => Subtype.eq (g.one_mul x.val)
  mul_one := fun x => Subtype.eq (g.mul_one x.val)
  mul_assoc := fun x y z => Subtype.eq (g.mul_assoc x.val y.val z.val)
  inv_mul := fun x => Subtype.eq (g.inv_mul x.val)

end Theory

import Base
namespace Tasks
inductive Word (G : Type) where
  | unit : Word G
  | atom : G → Word G
  | product : Word G → Word G → Word G
  | inverse : Word G → Word G

def Word.eval {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) : Word G → G
  | .unit => g.one
  | .atom x => x
  | .product x y => g.mul (x.eval g) (y.eval g)
  | .inverse x => g.inv (x.eval g)

def Word.admissible {G : Type} (p : G → Prop) : Word G → Prop
  | .unit => True
  | .atom x => p x
  | .product x y => x.admissible p ∧ y.admissible p
  | .inverse x => x.admissible p

def words : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) (g : Foundation.Group G) (h : Foundation.Group H)
    (f : G → H) (_hf : ∀ x y, f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y))
    (w : Word G), w.admissible (fun x => f x = h.one) → f (w.eval g) = h.one
end Tasks

namespace GroupFacts

theorem left_cancel {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (a b c : G)
    (e : g.mul a b = g.mul a c) : b = c := by
  calc
    b = g.mul g.one b := (g.one_mul b).symm
    _ = g.mul (g.mul (g.inv a) a) b :=
      congrArg (fun z => g.mul z b) (g.inv_mul a).symm
    _ = g.mul (g.inv a) (g.mul a b) := g.mul_assoc (g.inv a) a b
    _ = g.mul (g.inv a) (g.mul a c) := congrArg (g.mul (g.inv a)) e
    _ = g.mul (g.mul (g.inv a) a) c := (g.mul_assoc (g.inv a) a c).symm
    _ = g.mul g.one c := congrArg (fun z => g.mul z c) (g.inv_mul a)
    _ = c := g.one_mul c

theorem mul_inv {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (x : G) :
    g.mul x (g.inv x) = g.one := by
  apply left_cancel g (g.inv x)
  calc
    g.mul (g.inv x) (g.mul x (g.inv x)) =
        g.mul (g.mul (g.inv x) x) (g.inv x) :=
      (g.mul_assoc (g.inv x) x (g.inv x)).symm
    _ = g.mul g.one (g.inv x) := congrArg (fun z => g.mul z (g.inv x)) (g.inv_mul x)
    _ = g.inv x := g.one_mul (g.inv x)
    _ = g.mul (g.inv x) g.one := (g.mul_one (g.inv x)).symm

theorem inv_one {G : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) : g.inv g.one = g.one :=
  (g.mul_one (g.inv g.one)).symm.trans (g.inv_mul g.one)

end GroupFacts

theorem Hom.map_one {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : f.toFun g.one = h.one := by
  apply GroupFacts.left_cancel h (f.toFun g.one)
  calc
    h.mul (f.toFun g.one) (f.toFun g.one) = f.toFun (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
      (f.map_mul g.one g.one).symm
    _ = f.toFun g.one := congrArg f.toFun (g.one_mul g.one)
    _ = h.mul (f.toFun g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f.toFun g.one)).symm

  apply GroupFacts.left_cancel h (f.toFun x)

1. Read the condition, original goal, supplied modules and budgets. Treat the goal and foundation as fixed. In baseline, use only the supplied foundation; in treatment, candidate definitions and proved lemmas are available. Never import a larger library or add axioms.
2. Identify the proof obligation in the original vocabulary. For treatment, inspect candidate definitions and find a representation bridge: bundle raw data, prove its structure fields, transport hypotheses, use a candidate property, and return to the original goal. A short definitional bridge can suffice. If the package does not help, prove directly and say so.
3. Write a Lean term after the controller-owned declaration's := delimiter, usually a by block. Put any helper lemma inside this term. Do not edit frozen files, replace the theorem statement, alter checker options or reset the attempt budget.
4. Explain the bridge in a short text file. State which candidate properties are used and where raw hypotheses discharge their preconditions. Do not invent a successful compilation.
5. Package the response with the bundled script:

~~~bash
python /path/to/evaluate-theory-package/scripts/pack_submission.py \
  --request request.json --proof proof.lean --bridge bridge.txt \
  --output submission.json
~~~

The proof file contains only the term, not imports or a theorem wrapper. The script checks request/source fingerprints and response size; it does not run Lean.

6. Return submission.json to the controller. If given verification feedback, inspect the exact failure and revise within the remaining attempt count. Treat timeouts, interruptions and unsolved tasks as unknown under a budget. Stop when the controller reports exhaustion. Never hide or erase failed attempts.
7. Report separately: supplied proof, submitted attempt, verified witness, or no verified witness observed. A JSON response or successful packaging is not proof verification.

## Controller steps

1. Locate the requested MAAM checkout. Read its docs/MIGRATION_PROTOCOL.md and suite manifest. Use a candidate frozen before evaluation. If changing it after development feedback, create a new package/suite version and new sessions; never silently refresh hashes.
2. Start baseline and treatment with the same explicit solver identity, mode and suite. For example:

~~~bash
python -m maam migration-start --suite experiments/hom_kernel_migration/suite.json \
  --session data/run-baseline --condition baseline --solver-id solver-version
python -m maam migration-start --suite experiments/hom_kernel_migration/suite.json \
  --session data/run-treatment --condition treatment --solver-id solver-version
python -m maam migration-request --session data/run-treatment \
  --task d01 --output request.json
~~~

3. Give a fresh worker only the request and skill. Do not supply intended proofs or the other condition's feedback. Record model/version, prompt, sampling settings, task order and actual generation usage externally. The runner enforces submission and Lean verification budgets; it cannot independently meter an external model's generation budget.
4. Submit the worker artifact:

~~~bash
python -m maam migration-submit --session data/run-treatment \
  --submission submission.json --output attempt-report.json
~~~

Read the returned status and retained command logs. Use a new report filename for each attempt. Lean and the auditor must accept the original proposition and dependency policy before calling an attempt verified. The CLI writes a failed report before returning a nonzero exit code.

5. Summarize and compare:

~~~bash
python -m maam migration-report --session data/run-treatment --output session-report.json
python -m maam migration-compare --baseline data/run-baseline \
  --treatment data/run-treatment --output comparison.json
~~~

Compare coverage separately from cost on common solved tasks. Charge all candidate source once. Do not interpret a local proof-body saving, an unsolved task, or a supplied calibration proof as an independently established preference or a general interest score.

6. Keep the candidate fixed when inspecting reserved results. Public reference proofs make the bundled suite calibration material. Independent held-out evidence requires a separate controlled run with recorded information boundaries; this release always marks held_out_evaluation and training_eligible false.

Read [protocol.md](references/protocol.md) for statuses, interruption handling and scope.

# Protocol details

- Keep the controller's session directory private from task-local workers. The request exports only the current task and condition. This is an information-boundary procedure, not filesystem access control.
- Use Lean 4.24.0 for the bundled suite. Install and warm the pinned toolchain before timed verification; otherwise a download can consume verification time.
- Submission fields: task_id, request_sha256, proof, bridge; optional generation is caller-reported metadata. Extra fields cannot alter targets or budgets.
- verified means the Lean witness and module/axiom/goal audit passed. rejected means compilation or the formal policy failed. inconclusive means a resource limit or environment/controller problem prevented verification.
- A pending attempt without a result is incomplete and still consumes its slot. If the controller died while holding controller.lock, inspect the process and pending artifacts before removing that stale lock. Preserve the attempt directory.
- Attempt records, source bytes and full command stdout/stderr have SHA-256 checks. These detect accidental edits; they are unsigned local records, not tamper-proof attestations.
- Use fresh directories for each condition and attempt. Precompiled local objects and the opposite condition's library are not copied into verification.
- Source costs count parsed Lean tokens in every nonshared proof module plus the whole candidate once. The common foundation and unchanged task statements cancel. Elaborated local expression sizes do not expand referenced lemmas.
- The runner selects the smallest observed full proof-module source among verified in-budget attempts; this is not a global minimum proof.
- Lean source can execute metaprograms. Run only trusted inputs here; hostile inputs require a separate OS/container sandbox without credentials.
- This skill performs evidence collection. Package ablations, independent held-out validation and a learning-algorithm-specific feedback policy are separate experimental stages.
